exposure: Mode of delivery (successful VE vs. failed VE)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies delivered at term by failed vacuum extraction (n=4747) or successful vacuum extraction (n=83,671) in Sweden between 1999 and 2010
finding: Failed vacuum extraction was associated with an increased risk of neonatal complications, such as subgaleal hemorrhage, convulsions, and low Apgar scores, compared to successful vacuum extraction.
mod_finding: Infants delivered by failed vacuum extraction had a higher risk of subgaleal hemorrhage, convulsions, and low Apgar scores, but not intracranial hemorrhage, compared to those delivered by successful vacuum extraction.
